hero.heading: Aurelia Residences

hero.nightImageAlt: The courtyard at dusk, pool lights on and residences lit against the night sky.

hotspots.label: Light through the rooms
hotspots.description: Every primary room turns toward the inlet, so the day is read in reflections.

hotspots.label: Stone that lasts
hotspots.description: Limewashed stone and dark timber, chosen to weather the salt rather than stay new.

hotspots.label: The quiet street wall
hotspots.description: From the road, only a timber wall and a single opening. The water is kept for the people who live here.

arch.label: Into the three reasons to return

story.tagline: A place to live — and to come back to.
story.heading: Boutique Concept
story.caption: Designed as a community, not a complex.

beats.title: Boutique Concept
beats.body: A boutique gated community of eighteen residences, designed around privacy, wellbeing and quiet harbour living.
beats.imageAlt: The courtyard and residences in afternoon light.

beats.title: Built to Stay
beats.body: Stone, timber and a courtyard that will take the weather. The houses are made to be lived in for decades, not seasons.
beats.imageAlt: A quiet living room — a house, not a corridor of doors.

beats.title: Made to Return
beats.body: Rooms turn toward the water, so the day is read in reflections rather than in a corridor of doors.
beats.imageAlt: The courtyard at dusk, pool lights on and residences lit.

vista.quote: Instead of corridors, walking paths connect the residences — making Aurelia feel closer to a group of private homes than a complex.
vista.imageAlt: A stone residence with flowering vines beside a still pool and palms.

intro.body: Aurelia stands on the north bank, above a harbour that still works for a living. Eighteen residences, three storeys, one stair. Nothing rises above the pines behind it.
intro.aside: Laid along the bank rather than across it.

poles.label: The quay
poles.body: Boat sheds, a fuel pump, the six o'clock ferry. The water is in use from first light, and the building sits close enough to hear it.

poles.label: The treeline
poles.body: Spruce and birch hold the slope behind. The last residence stops where the ridge path starts, and the ground is left as it was found.

between.imageAlt: A timber jetty on still water, with a treeline along the far shore.

route.heading: Eleven minutes, end to end
route.body: Everything the harbour keeps sits inside a short walk. The line below follows the way it is walked, along the water and up into the trees.
route.footnote: Times measured from the north entrance, at walking pace.

location.description: A working harbour of two thousand people. Aurelia stands on the last ridge before the water, eight minutes above the quay.
location.imageAlt: Aerial view of the shoreline, with the residences along the beach and the hills behind.

interiors.body: Oak floors, lime plaster, deep sills. The rooms were drawn long, so the light has somewhere to travel before it reaches the far wall.

architecture.heading: Stone that remembers the tide.
architecture.quote: We kept the rooms long and the openings few, so the house would feel like it had always been looking at the water.
architecture.materials: Dark timber, limewashed stone, and bronze that will dull in the salt air. Nothing that asks to stay new.

assurance.heading: The facts behind the drawings
assurance.intro: Who is building Aurelia, where the permits stand, and what has been poured so far. Every line here can be checked against a document.

rows.title: The developer
rows.detail: Aurelia is built by Halvard Estate, a family firm working this coastline since 1994. Eleven completed schemes, none of them larger than twenty-four homes. The same site manager has run the last four.

rows.title: Sales and marketing
rows.detail: Sales are handled by Meridian Harbour Partners from the office at 12 Harbor Path. One team, one price list, no intermediaries. Viewings are booked for the morning, when the light is on the water.

rows.title: Planning and permits
rows.detail: Outline consent was granted in March 2025 under reference NH/2025/0148. The building permit followed that June, with no conditions outstanding. Both documents travel with the reservation pack.

rows.title: Construction status
rows.detail: The frame is complete to the third floor and the roof closes in spring. First handovers are set for autumn 2027. A camera on the east crane runs through daylight hours.

rows.title: Deposits and warranty
rows.detail: Deposits are held in a client account at Nordbank and released against certified stages. Each residence carries a ten-year structural warranty and two years on the finishes.

image.alt: The north elevation in flat daylight, concrete frame and deep window reveals.
image.caption: North elevation, September.

residenceFigures.body: Two, three and four bedrooms, each with its own outdoor room — a garden at the lower level, a terrace in the middle, a solarium at the top.

closingView.body: The slope does the work. Every residence sits half a level above the one in front of it, so the harbour is never somebody else's view.

map.alt: A cool northern inlet seen from above, dark water against a wooded shore.

footer.ctaSubheading: A short conversation is enough to know if it fits.
